exposure: False diagnosis of fetal growth restriction
cohort: 34,474 singleton term deliveries of appropriately grown fetuses (10-90th weight percentiles) in a single medical center (2007-2014), excluding elective cesarean-section, diabetes, and hypertension
finding: False diagnosis of fetal growth restriction is associated with higher rates of induction of labor, cesarean deliveries, and short-term adverse neonatal outcomes, even in appropriately grown fetuses.
